:::{#thm-norm-properties}
#### Basic properties of the Euclidean norm

For any $\vecf{x} \in \reals^p$ and any number $c$:

1. $\norm{\vecf{x}} \ge 0$, and $\norm{\vecf{x}} = 0$ if and only if $\vecf{x} = \vzero$;
2. $\norm{c\,\vecf{x}} = \abs{c}\,\norm{\vecf{x}}$.

:::

::: proof

**Part 1.**
$\norm{\vecf{x}} = \sqrt{x_1^2 + \cdots + x_p^2}$ (@eq-l2-norm)
is the square root of a sum of squares, so it is at least $0$.
It is $0$ exactly when $x_1^2 + \cdots + x_p^2 = 0$,
and a sum of squares is $0$ exactly when every term is $0$,
that is, when every $x_i = 0$:
if some $x_i \ne 0$, its square is positive and the sum is positive,
and if every $x_i = 0$, the sum is $0$.

**Part 2.**

$$
\ba
\norm{c\,\vecf{x}}
&= \sqrt{\sumip (c\,x_i)^2}
&& \text{(@eq-l2-norm, and @def-scalar-mult)}
\\
&= \sqrt{\sumip c^2 x_i^2}
&& \text{(} (c\,x_i)^2 = c^2 x_i^2 \text{)}
\\
&= \sqrt{c^2 \sumip x_i^2}
&& \text{(factor } c^2 \text{ out of the sum)}
\\
&= \sqrt{c^2}\,\sqrt{\sumip x_i^2}
&& \text{(the square root of a product of nonnegative numbers)}
\\
&= \abs{c}\,\norm{\vecf{x}}.
&& \text{(} \sqrt{c^2} = \abs{c} \text{, and @eq-l2-norm)}
\ea
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-norm-properties}
#### Scaling a vector scales its length

For $\vecf{x} = (3, 4)$, $\norm{\vecf{x}} = 5$ (@exm-euclidean-norm).
Then $-2\,\vecf{x} = (-6, -8)$ has norm
$\sqrt{36 + 64} = 10 = \abs{-2} \cd 5$,
as part 2 says.
Dividing by the norm gives a vector of length $1$:
$\norm{\tfrac{1}{5}\,\vecf{x}} = \tfrac{1}{5} \cd 5 = 1$,
and $\tfrac{1}{5}\,\vecf{x} = (0.6, 0.8)$ is the unit vector in @exm-euclidean-norm.

:::
